I will mostly do what has worked for me around here, then make a few small adjustments. I have 13.1 mu, and with wheat-maize being my main way of planting, I will keep most of the land in that rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Last year, the wheat-maize land gave me steadier grain and easier sales, so I will put 10.0 mu into wheat, then follow it with 10.0 mu maize on the same land, and I will keep 3.1 mu for cotton. I only finished primary school, so I do not make it too fancy. I look at what I did before, what the neighbors nearby do when they get a decent harvest, and what I can afford. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing yield is worse, so I will not cut too hard. With well irrigation, I will make sure wheat gets water at the key times, maize gets watered in the hot period if rain is short, and cotton gets enough to hold squares and bolls. For seed, I will use improved wheat, hybrid maize, and improved cotton because I have seen those do better in the village. I will keep pesticide use practical: a couple of sprays on wheat and maize, more on cotton because insects are usually more troublesome there. For tillage, I will keep it simple and use rotary tillage where it saves labor, and no-tillage maize after wheat if the soil moisture is right.
